sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Core Java interview questions are the foundation of every Java backend interview. This page covers the language fundamentals interviewers actually probe — exception handling (checked vs unchecked, try-with-resources), generics and type erasure, reflection, the Java I/O and NIO APIs, string immutability, and the small comparisons that recur in every loop (== vs equals, Comparable vs Comparator, abstract class vs interface). For pure object-oriented design questions (encapsulation, polymorphism, SOLID applied to Java) head to the dedicated Java OOP page. Each answer is structured the way you would actually answer in a 45-minute interview: the headline, the why, a code-shaped example, and the trade-off the interviewer is really listening for.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Three layers, **always the same**:

1. **Language semantics** — pass-by-value, equals/hashCode, immutability, the type system.
2. **Runtime model** — heap vs stack, the GC root set, the class loader chain.
3. **API contracts** — `Optional`, `try-with-resources`, generics + erasure, reflection.

Senior interviewers test you at the **boundary** between these layers (e.g. why `==` on autoboxed `Integer` 127 ≠ 128, why generic arrays are illegal, why `String` is immutable).

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Comparisons** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Exception handling** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Generics wildcards** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Java io nio** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Reflection annotations** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **String handling** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **`equals` / `hashCode` contract** — break it and `HashMap` silently misbehaves; mention it before the interviewer prompts you.
- **Type erasure** — name `ClassCastException` at runtime as the cost; mention `TypeToken` / `Class<T>` workarounds.
- **Pass-by-value** — Java *only*. Reference values are copied; the object is shared. Be ready with an example of a mutable parameter inside a method.
- **`final` vs `finally` vs `finalize`** — three different things; `finalize` is deprecated since 9.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"In Java the contract is X — here's the language guarantee, here's how the JVM implements it, and here's the one place it bites: <named exception> when <named edge case>. The fix is <pattern> — for instance Y in our codebase used <approach> to keep <equals/hashCode | immutability | type-safety> intact."*
